payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to the requested jacket closure only. Return yes if support 1 passes: the jacket is fully closed. Return no if support 1 fails and support 2 fails: no requested change has progressed. Return partial if support 1 fails and support 2 passes: some progress is visible but the jacket is not fully closed. Return unknown if support 1 is unknown, or if support 1 fails and support 2 is unknown. Support 2 is skipped when support 1 passes; on that path, the directly observed fully closed endpoint establishes completion without a progress comparison. A skipped support is unobserved, not a negative finding. Unrelated edits do not count as progress, and supporting evidence alone does not earn completion credit.
node.binding: Target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.. Reference: The woman's jacket in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: Support 1 fails: the jacket is not fully closed. Support 2 is unknown, so whether any progress toward closing it occurred cannot be established.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image shows the jacket hanging open, with a clear gap between the front panels.
The woman’s pose and the jacket’s draping differ substantially between images. The front closure area is not reliably comparable, so visible progress toward closing the jacket cannot be established.

response.content: {"text":"The endpoint check is well grounded: the edited image shows the jacket open, so support 1 should remain a failure. The unresolved result comes from support 2’s comparison, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Improve the node’s binding/criteria so progress is judged from the visible jacket closure itself, using the source and edited images while accounting for pose and drape changes; compare whether the front panels or closure have moved toward each other, and return unknown only when that evidence genuinely cannot be assessed. Do not infer progress merely from the jacket’s changed appearance or force the reference label: the images show a substantial pose change and the edited jacket hanging open, so the evidence may still warrant uncertainty about progress."}
